FT​U,Tcos⁡(2​ϕ^h−ϕS−ϕ^Sh)​(zh,j⟂)\displaystyle F^{\cos(2 \hat{\phi}_h - \phi_S - \hat{\phi}_{S_h})}_{TU,T}(z_{h},j_{\perp}) =−𝒞​[j⟂22​zh2​Mh2​h1​f1​ℋ1​T⟂​ΔT​σ^].\displaystyle=-\mathcal{C}\bqty{\frac{j^2_{\perp}}{2 z_h^2 M_h^2} h_{1} f_1 \mathcal{H}_{1 T}^{\perp} \Delta_T \hat{\sigma}}\,. (169)

The corresponding polarizations for hard functions σ^a​bc\hat{\sigma}_{ab}^{c}, Δ​σ^a​bc\Delta\hat{\sigma}_{ab}^{c} and ΔT​σ^a​bc\Delta_{T}\hat{\sigma}_{ab}^{c} are given in Table 2. The expressions for FU​U,UF_{UU,U} and FU​U,Tsin⁡(ϕ^h−ϕ^Sh)F^{\sin(\hat{\phi}_h - \hat{\phi}_{S_h})}_{UU,T} were given in the previous publication [34] while [91] performed a phenomenological study for FT​U,Usin⁡(ϕS−ϕ^h)F^{\sin(\phi_S - \hat{\phi}_h)}_{TU,U}, that is related to the Collins TMD FFs. The detailed expressions for all the other structure functions are written down here for the first time.

Relevant measurements have been performed for the π±\pi^{\pm}-in-jet production in the case of Collins FFs [102]. More relevantly, a measurement of transverse spin transfer to Λ/Λ¯\Lambda/\overline{\Lambda} hyperons in polarized p​ppp collisions (no jet is involved) was performed by the STAR collaboration at RHIC [103]. This suggests that measuring the transverse polarization of Λ/Λ¯\Lambda/\overline{\Lambda} hyperons inside the jet in transversely polarized p​ppp collisions could be achieved at RHIC. This process would correspond to the structure function FT​U,Tcos⁡(ϕS−ϕ^Sh)F^{\cos(\phi_S - \hat{\phi}_{S_h})}_{TU,T}, which is sensitive to both transversity PDFs h1h_{1} and transversity TMD FJFs ℋ1h/q\mathcal{H}_{1}^{h/q}. Below, we focus on this structure function and define the following spin asymmetry for Λ\Lambda-in-jet productions:

AT​U,Tcos⁡(ϕS−ϕ^Sh)≡FT​U,Tcos⁡(ϕS−ϕ^Sh)/FU​U,U.\displaystyle A_{TU,T}^{\cos(\phi_S - \hat{\phi}_{S_h})}\equiv F_{TU,T}^{\cos(\phi_S - \hat{\phi}_{S_h})}\bigg/F_{UU,U}\,. (174)

In order to compute FT​U,Tcos⁡(ϕ^h−ϕ^Sh)F_{TU,T}^{\cos(\hat{\phi}_h - \hat{\phi}_{S_h})}, we will need to parameterize the collinear transversity PDF h1​(x,μ)h_{1}(x,\mu), which appears in the initial state of FT​U,Tcos⁡(ϕS−ϕ^Sh)F_{TU,T}^{\cos(\phi_S - \hat{\phi}_{S_h})} in Eq. 168. For this, we follow the parameterization in [104] and write the quark transversity as:

h1q​(x,Q0)=Nqh​xaq​(1−x)bq​(aq+bq)aq+bqaqaq​bqbq​12​(f1q​(x,Q0)+g1q​(x,Q0)),h_{1}^{q}\pqty{x, Q_0}=N_{q}^{h}x^{a_{q}}\pqty{1 - x}^{b_{q}}\frac{\pqty{a_q + b_q}^{a_{q}+b_{q}}}{a_{q}^{a_{q}}b_{q}^{b_{q}}}\frac{1}{2}\pqty{f_1^q \pqty{x, Q_0} + g_1^q \pqty{x, Q_0}}\,, (175)

at initial scale Q0=1.27​GeVQ_{0}=1.27~\mathrm{GeV}, for up and down quarks q=uq=u and dd only. The f1qf_{1}^{q} and g1qg_{1}^{q} are the collinear unpolarized and helicity parton distributions respectively, for which we use the parameters from [105]. Lastly, in the generation of TMD FFs grids, we also need the transversity FFs. In this work we use the parameterization from [42], which assumes a simple normalization of the collinear unpolarized FFs:

HΛ/q​(z,Q)=NqH​DΛ/q​(z,Q).H_{\Lambda/q}\pqty{z, Q}=N_{q}^{H}D_{\Lambda/q}\pqty{z, Q}\,. (176)

Here HΛ/qH_{\Lambda/q} and DΛ/qD_{\Lambda/q} are the transversity and unpolarized FFs of the Λ\Lambda baryon, and NqHN_{q}^{H} is the fitted parameter. We also follow the assumptions made in [106, 42] and demand:

DΛ/q=DΛ¯/q=12​DΛ/Λ¯←q,D_{\Lambda/q}=D_{\overline{\Lambda}/q}=\frac{1}{2}D_{\Lambda/\overline{\Lambda}\leftarrow q}\,, (177)

as for the unpolarized Λ\Lambda baryon FFs that appear in the denominator of AT​U,Tcos⁡(ϕS−ϕ^Sh)A_{TU,T}^{\cos(\phi_S - \hat{\phi}_{S_h})}, we use the AKK parametrization [107]. For both the transversity PDFs and transversity FFs, we also vary their fitted parameters according to the extracted uncertainties, weighted by Gaussian random number with a mean of 0 and variance of 1.

Using the above setup, we now present the first prediction for the spin asymmetry AT​U,Tcos⁡(ϕS−ϕ^Sh)A_{TU,T}^{\cos(\phi_S - \hat{\phi}_{S_h})}. We choose the jet kinematics consistent with the available data from STAR [102], with the center of mass energy at s=200​GeV\sqrt{s}=200~\mathrm{GeV}, rapidity ranges η∈(0,0.9)\eta\in\pqty{0, 0.9} and η∈(−0.9,0)\eta\in\pqty{-0.9, 0}. The jets are reconstructed using the anti-kTk_{T} algorithm with radius R=0.6R=0.6. The numerical implementation is very similar to that used in the longitudinal momentum distribution of hadrons inside jets [21], with the numerical DGLAP evolution tool developed in Pegasus [108]. The RG evolution of the various parts of the cross sections is performed as outlined in [23].

In Fig. 6, the prediction to AT​U,Tcos⁡(ϕS−ϕ^Sh)A_{TU,T}^{\cos(\phi_S - \hat{\phi}_{S_h})} for the jet(Λ)(\Lambda) production at RHIC kinematics is presented. The blue band is obtained by varying the fitted parameters of both transversity PDFs and transversity FFs, while the yellow band is obtained by varying the parameters of transversity PDFs only (with parameters for transversity FFs fixed at central values). We can therefore deduce that the uncertainty of theoretical prediction for the observable AT​U,Tcos⁡(ϕS−ϕ^Sh)A_{TU,T}^{\cos(\phi_S - \hat{\phi}_{S_h})} comes largely from the transversity FFs, i.e., variation of NqHN_{q}^{H} in Eq. 176. Given the large uncertainty resulting from the currently available extraction of the transversity FFs for Λ\Lambda baryon, this observable, when measured in the future, can be used to constrain the uncertainty on the Λ\Lambda transversity FFs.

In Fig. 7, the same predictions are presented but with a negative rapidity range. Similar patterns occur as in Fig. 6, but with a much smaller magnitude, indicating a much smaller probability of producing polarized final particles in the opposite direction of the polarized beam.

Overall, in proton-proton collisions for Λ\Lambda-in-jet production, where one of the proton beams is transversely polarized, and the resulting Lambda particles in the jet also exhibit transverse polarization, a distinct observation emerges. Specifically, in the forward region (positive rapidity), a moderate spin asymmetry AT​U,Tcos⁡(ϕS−ϕ^Sh)∼1.5%A_{TU,T}^{\cos(\phi_S - \hat{\phi}_{S_h})}\sim 1.5\% can be observed at RHIC kinematics, while in the backward region (negative rapidity), the spin asymmetry AT​U,Tcos⁡(ϕS−ϕ^Sh)A_{TU,T}^{\cos(\phi_S - \hat{\phi}_{S_h})} appears to be very small. This is largely due to the probing xx range for the transversity PDF h1​(x,μ)h_{1}(x,\mu): in the forward rapidity region x∼0.2x\sim 0.2 at pT∼15p_{T}\sim 15 GeV where h1​(x,μ)h_{1}(x,\mu) is sizable [104]; in the backward rapidity region x∼0.05x\sim 0.05 for pT∼15p_{T}\sim 15 GeV where h1​(x,μ)h_{1}(x,\mu) is very small.

4.2 Back-to-back electron-jet production with longitudinally polarized Λ\Lambda in jet

For exclusive jet production, we choose to study back-to-back electron-jet production in deep inelastic e​pep scattering:

e​(ℓ,λe)+p​(P,S)→e​(ℓ′)+[jet⁡(pJ)​h​(zh,𝒋⟂,Sh)]+X,e\pqty{\ell, \lambda_e}+p\pqty{P, S}\to e\pqty{\ell'}+\bqty{\mathrm{jet}(p_J) h\pqty{z_h, \boldsymbol{j}_{\perp}, S_h}}+X\,, (178)

where ℓ\ell and ℓ′\ell^{\prime} are the momenta of the incident and scattered lepton respectively. The incident electron could carry a helicity λe\lambda_{e} and the scattered lepton is assumed to be unpolarized but with a transverse momentum ℓT′\bm{\ell}^{\prime}_{T}. Here we use PP and SS to represent the momentum and polarization of the incoming proton, and the jet has a momentum pJp_{J} with transverse component 𝒑T\bm{p}_{T}. The hadron inside the jet has a transverse momentum 𝒋⟂\bm{j}_{\perp} with respect to the jet axis and collinear momentum fraction zhz_{h} of the jet, as well as a polarization 𝑺h\bm{S}_{h} with respect to the jet axis. The kinematics is shown in Fig. 8. In the back-to-back region where |𝒒T|≪|𝒑T|\absolutevalue{\boldsymbol{q}_T}\ll\absolutevalue{\boldsymbol{p}_T} with the transverse momentum imbalance 𝒒T≡ℓT′+𝒑T\bm{q}_{T}\equiv\bm{\ell}^{\prime}_{T}+\bm{p}_{T}, TMD factorization formalism for the full differential cross section has been given in the previous publication [41], where various structure functions were defined and studied. For example, the structure function FU​U,Ucos⁡(ϕq−ϕ^h)F_{UU,U}^{\cos(\phi_q - \hat{\phi}_h)} for π±\pi^{\pm}-in-jet production is sensitive to Boer-Mulder function and Collins function, while FU​U,Tcos⁡(ϕ^h−ϕ^Sh)F_{UU,T}^{\cos(\hat{\phi}_h - \hat{\phi}_{S_h})} from Λ\Lambda-in-jet production has the sensitivity to the polarizing TMD FFs D1​T⊥D_{1T}^{\bot}. At the same time, in [93], the structure function FT​U,Usin⁡(ϕS−ϕ^h)F_{TU,U}^{\,\sin(\phi_{S} - \hat{\phi}_h)} is computed for π+/−\pi^{+/-}-in-jet production, and is found to be able to further constrain the Collins FFs.

In this section, we studied yet another observable - the spin asymmetry AT​U,Lcos⁡(ϕq−ϕS)A_{TU,L}^{\cos(\phi_q - \phi_{S})} defined as

AT​U,Lcos⁡(ϕq−ϕS)≡FT​U,Lcos⁡(ϕq−ϕS)FU​U,U,\displaystyle A_{TU,L}^{\cos(\phi_q - \phi_{S})}\equiv\frac{F_{TU,L}^{\cos(\phi_q - \phi_{S})}}{F_{UU,U}}\,, (179)

where the structure FT​U,Lcos⁡(ϕq−ϕS)F_{TU,L}^{\cos(\phi_q - \phi_{S})} in the numerator denotes the spin-dependent structure functions, with TT, UU and LL being the polarization of incoming proton, incoming electron, and the final-state hadron inside the jet, respectively. Here, ϕS\phi_{S} is the angle between the transverse spin of the incoming proton 𝑺T\bm{S}_{T} and the xx-axis, while ϕq\phi_{q} is the azimuthal angle between the transverse momentum imbalance 𝒒T\bm{q}_{T} and the xx-axis, see Fig. 8. Following [41], this structure function can be factorized as follows:

FT​U,Lcos⁡(ϕq−ϕS)​(zh,j⟂)\displaystyle F_{TU,L}^{\cos(\phi_q - \phi_{S})}(z_{h},j_{\perp}) =σ^0​H​(Q,μ)​∑qeq2​𝒢1​Lh/q​(zh,𝒋⟂,pT​R,μ,ζJ)\displaystyle=\hat{\sigma}_{0}H\pqty{Q, \mu}\sum_{q}e_{q}^{2}\mathscr{G}_{1L}^{h/q}\pqty{z_h, \boldsymbol{j}_{\perp}, p_T R, \mu, \zeta_J}
×∫b2​db2​π​J1​(qT​b)​x​M​g~1​T(1)​q​(x,𝒃,μ,ζ)​S¯global​(b2,μ)​S¯cs​(b2,R,μ),\displaystyle\times\int\frac{b^{2}\differential{b}}{2\pi}J_{1}\pqty{q_T b}xM\,\widetilde{g}_{1T}^{(1)q}\pqty{x, \boldsymbol{b}, \mu, \zeta}\overline{S}_{\mathrm{global}}\pqty{b^2 , \mu}\overline{S}_{\mathrm{cs}}\pqty{b^2 , R , \mu}\,, (180)

where the global soft function S¯global\overline{S}_{\mathrm{global}} and the collinear-soft function S¯cs\overline{S}_{\mathrm{cs}} are given in [41]. The bar in S¯global/cs\overline{S}_{\mathrm{global}/\mathrm{cs}} indicates that their dependence on azimuthal angle is averaged. σ^0\hat{\sigma}_{0} is the partonic cross section of electron-quark scattering:

σ^0=αem​αss^​Q2​2​(u^2+s^2)t^2,\hat{\sigma}_{0}=\frac{\alpha_{\mathrm{em}}\alpha_{s}}{\hat{s}Q^{2}}\frac{2\pqty{\hat{u}^2 + \hat{s}^2}}{\hat{t}^{2}}\,, (181)

with the Mandelstam variables s^≡(x​P+ℓ)2\hat{s}\equiv\pqty{xP + \ell}^{2}, t^≡(ℓ−ℓ′)2\hat{t}\equiv\pqty{\ell- \ell'}^{2} and u^≡(x​P−ℓ′)2\hat{u}\equiv\pqty{xP - \ell'}^{2}, where xx is the fraction of collinear momentum carried by the parton inside the incoming proton. The electromagnetic and strong coupling constants are denoted as αem\alpha_{\mathrm{em}} and αs\alpha_{s}, and the virtuality of the exchanged photon is defined as Q2≡−(ℓ−ℓ′)2=−t^Q^{2}\equiv-\pqty{\ell- \ell'}^{2}=-\hat{t}.

It is evident from Eq. 180 that this spin asymmetry AT​U,Lcos⁡(ϕq−ϕS)A_{TU,L}^{\cos(\phi_q - \phi_{S})} has sensitivity on both “worm-gear” TMD PDFs g~1​Tq​(x,𝒃,μ,ζ)\widetilde{g}_{1T}^{q}\pqty{x, \boldsymbol{b}, \mu, \zeta}, as well as the longitudinally polarized exclusive TMD FJFs 𝒢1​L​(zh,𝒋⟂,pT​R,μ,ζJ)\mathscr{G}_{1L}\pqty{z_h, \boldsymbol{j}_{\perp}, p_T R, \mu, \zeta_J} in Eq. 145, which is connected to the helicity TMD FFs G1​Lh/qG_{1L}^{h/q}. The observable describes the following scattering process: a longitudinally polarized quark inside the transversely polarized proton (as denoted by the TMD PDFs g1​Tqg_{1T}^{q}) scatters with an unpolarized electron and then initiates a jet in which a longitudinally polarized hadron is observed. To generate a prediction, for the first moment of “worm-gear” distribution g~1​T(1)​q\widetilde{g}_{1T}^{(1)q}, we adopt its parameterization in 𝒌⟂\bm{k}_{\perp}-space from [109], and Fourier transform it to the conjugate 𝒃\bm{b}-space:

g~1​T(1)​q​(x,𝒃,μ,ζ)=2​πM2​∫dk⟂​k⟂2b​J1​(k⟂​b)​g1​Tq​(x,𝒌⟂2)=g1​T(1)​q​(x)​exp⁡(−14​b2​⟨k⟂2⟩|g1​Tq),\widetilde{g}_{1T}^{(1)q}\pqty{x, \boldsymbol{b}, \mu, \zeta}=\frac{2\pi}{M^{2}}\int\differential{k}_{\perp}\frac{{k}_{\perp}^{2}}{b}J_{1}({k}_{\perp}b)g_{1T}^{q}(x,\bm{k}_{\perp}^{2})=g_{1T}^{\pqty{1}q}\pqty{x}\exp(-\frac{1}{4} b^2 \langle k_{\perp}^2\rangle\big|_{g_{1T}^q})\,, (182)

where M≈938.272​MeVM\approx 938.272~\mathrm{MeV} is the proton mass and g1​T(1)​q​(x)g_{1T}^{\pqty{1}q}\pqty{x} is the collinear function that is parameterized at Q0=2​GeVQ_{0}=2~\mathrm{GeV} [109]. Note that this is a simple parton model extraction without TMD evolution, we thus also do not take into account TMD evolution for g~1​Tq\widetilde{g}_{1T}^{q}. Since CT10 PDFs [110] are used in the extraction of g~1​Tq\widetilde{g}_{1T}^{q}, we will use them in the computation of FU​U,UF_{UU,U} as well. For the final-state hadron, we observe the longitudinally polarized Λ/Λ¯\Lambda/\overline{\Lambda} production. The corresponding helicity TMD FFs is given by:

G~1​LΛ/q​(zh,𝒃,μ,ζJ)=G1​LΛ/q​(zh,μb∗)​exp⁡[∫μb∗μdμ′μ′​γμi​[αs​(μ),ζJ/μ2]]​SN​Pq​(b,Q0,ζJ),\displaystyle\widetilde{G}_{1L}^{\Lambda/q}\pqty{z_h, \boldsymbol{b}, \mu, \zeta_J}={G}_{1L}^{\Lambda/q}\pqty{z_h, \mu_{b_{*}}}\exp[\int_{\mu_{b_{*}}}^{\mu}\frac{\differential{\mu'}}{\mu^{\prime}}\gamma_{\mu}^{i}\bqty{\alpha_s(\mu), \zeta_J/\mu^2}]S_{NP}^{q}\pqty{b, Q_0, \sqrt{\zeta_J}}\,, (183)

where we use the TMD evolution in Eq. 97 and we assume the non-perturbative Sudakov is the same as the unpolarized case in Eq. 152 [111]. For the collinear helicity FFs for Λ/Λ¯\Lambda/\overline{\Lambda}, we take the parameterizations from [112], in which three scenarios are provided, each with a different assumption for the source of contribution to Λ\Lambda longitudinal polarization. Specifically,

  • •

    Scenario 1: only polarized ss quark contributes;

  • •

    Scenario 2: uu and dd quarks have equal contributions, while the distribution of ss quark has an opposite sign relative to uu and dd quarks; uu and dd helicity FFs are negative

  • •

    Scenario 3: uu, dd, and ss quarks have the same distribution functions, which are all positive.

With the above setup, we are able to make predictions for the exclusive process e​p→e+jet​(Λ/Λ¯)+Xep\to e+\mathrm{jet}\pqty{\Lambda/\overline{\Lambda}}+X, in which we measure the longitudinal polarization of the final state Λ/Λ¯\Lambda/\overline{\Lambda} inside the jet. In Fig. 9, we plot the spin asymmetry AT​U,Lcos⁡(ϕq−ϕS)A_{TU,L}^{\cos(\phi_q - \phi_{S})} defined in Eq. 179 with EIC kinematics, where s=105​GeV\sqrt{s}=105~\mathrm{GeV}, jet transverse momentum pT∈(10,15)​GeVp_{T}\in\pqty{10, 15}~\mathrm{GeV}, and jet radius parameter R=0.6R=0.6. We also introduce the quantity event inelasticity y=1−ℓT′s​e−ye∈(0.1,0.9)y=1-\frac{\ell_{T}^{\prime}}{\sqrt{s}}e^{-y_{e}}\in\pqty{0.1, 0.9}, where ℓT′\ell_{T}^{\prime} and yey_{e} are the measured transverse momentum and rapidity of the scattered electron. Constraining the event inelasticity ensures that our calculation stays in the region with reasonable resolution on xx and Q2Q^{2}, as well as avoiding the phase where QED radiative corrections are important [93]. On the left panel, we plot AT​U,Lcos⁡(ϕq−ϕS)A_{TU,L}^{\cos(\phi_q - \phi_{S})} as a function of hadron transverse momentum j⊥j_{\bot}, while on the right panel, we plot the same spin asymmetry as a function of the electron-jet transverse momentum imbalance qTq_{T}. For the j⊥j_{\bot}-distribution (left), qTq_{T} is chosen to be 0.5 GeV, while for the qTq_{T}-distribution (right), j⊥j_{\bot} is chosen to be 0.5 GeV. The uncertainty band is obtained by computing the 1-σ\sigma band of the fitted parameters for the “worm-gear” PDFs g1​Tg_{1T}, and the three scenarios for the helicity fragmentation functions of Λ/Λ¯\Lambda/\overline{\Lambda} are shown by blue (scenario 1), red (scenario 2) and green (scenario 3). We collectively denote Λ/Λ¯\Lambda/\overline{\Lambda} as Λ\Lambda.

As can be inferred from Fig. 9, the different scenarios for helicity FFs provided in [112] can result in drastically different values in AT​U,Lcos⁡(ϕq−ϕS)A_{TU,L}^{\cos(\phi_q - \phi_{S})}. Notably, Scenario 1 is consistent with zero because only the ss quark helicity FFs contribute in this scenario. However, the current extraction of the “worm-gear” function g1​T(1)​q​(x){g}_{1T}^{(1)q}(x) of the incident proton receives contributions solely from uu and dd quarks, and the ss quark worm-gear function vanish [109]. As for Scenarios 2 and 3, distinct measurable asymmetries emerge with different signs, simply because in Scenario 2, both uu and dd helicity FFs are both negative, while they are positive in Scenario 3. This observable thus enables the discrimination of previously indistinguishable helicity fragmentation functions for Λ/Λ¯\Lambda/\overline{\Lambda} from different quark flavors.

5 Conclusion

The study of fragmenting jet functions (FJFs) has become a topic of paramount importance in high-energy physics, particularly at the LHC and RHIC, where measurements have been made for a broad range of identified particles within jets. These studies not only provide crucial information at the LHC and RHIC, but also hold the potential to yield novel insights at the upcoming Electron-Ion Collider (EIC).

It is thus important to study both longitudinal and transverse momentum distribution of hadrons inside the jet, which are characterized by the so-called semi-inclusive fragmenting jet functions and exclusive fragmenting jet functions. They are critical ingredients in the factorization theorems. The semi-inclusive fragmenting jet functions arise in the situation e.g., single inclusive jet production in proton-proton or electron-proton collisions, while the exclusive fragmenting jet functions appear in the situation e.g., back-to-back electron-jet production in electron-proton collisions. There have been partial results available in previous publications, but never the complete full results, which we set up to do in this paper. In this work, we have studied the hadron longitudinal momentum fraction zhz_{h} distribution, as well as the hadron transverse momentum j⟂j_{\perp} distribution within jets, for both semi-inclusive and exclusive fragmenting jet functions. We set up factorization formalism within SCET framework that allows for the systematic determination of these distributions. We first calculated all the components of the factorization theorem up to NLO, then we resummed all the associated large logarithms ln⁡(R)\ln{R} and ln⁡(pT​R/j⟂)\ln(p_T R / j_{\perp}).

In the phenomenology for semi-inclusive process, we study the transverse polarization of Lambda hyperons inside the jet produced in transversely polarized proton-proton collisions, which is sensitive to the elusive TMD transversity fragmentation functions. Our numerical estimate shows that this observable is promising at the RHIC. For the exclusive jet production process, we study the longitudinal polarization of Lambda hyperon inside the jet, in the back-to-back electron-jet production in electron-proton collisions where the proton is transversely polarized. We find that this observable is sensitive to the “worm-gear” TMD PDF g1​Tg_{1T} and the TMD helicity fragmentation functions and its measurement is promising at the future EIC. With the various applications for probing the 3D QCD structures, the future for fragmenting jet observables is promising with all the planned measurements at the RHIC and the EIC.

As defined in Section 2.1.1, we have the leading order and one-loop bare semi-inclusive FJFs for longitudinally and transversely polarized quarks and gluons. To get the final expression as given in Eqs. 22, 23, 24, 25 and 27, we first perform the q⟂q_{\perp} integral:

1z2​ϵ\displaystyle\frac{1}{z^{2\epsilon}} =1−2​ϵ​ln⁡(z)+𝒪⁡(ϵ2),\displaystyle=1-2\epsilon\ln(z)+\order{\epsilon^2}\,, (187)
(eγE​μ2ωJ2​tan2(ℛ2))ϵ​1Γ​(1−ϵ)\displaystyle\pqty{\frac{e^{\gamma_E} \mu^2}{\omega_J^2 \tan[2](\frac{\mathcal{R}}{2})}}^{\epsilon}\frac{1}{\Gamma\pqty{1 - \epsilon}} =1+L​ϵ+112​(6​L2−π2)​ϵ2+𝒪⁡(ϵ3),\displaystyle=1+L\epsilon+\frac{1}{12}\pqty{6 L^2 - \pi^2}\epsilon^{2}+\order{\epsilon^3}\,, (188)

Appendix B Calculation of collinear exclusive FJFs

In this section, we provide the derivation for the matching coefficients Δ(T)​𝒥i​j\Delta_{(T)}\mathscr{J}_{ij} of the exclusive fragmenting jet functions Δ(T)​𝒢ih​(zh,pT​R,μ)\Delta_{(T)}\mathscr{G}_{i}^{h}(z_{h},p_{T}R,\mu) to the collinear fragmentation function Δ(T)​Dih​(zh,μ)\Delta_{(T)}D_{i}^{h}(z_{h},\mu) for anti-kT{k}_{T} jets. The unpolarized results were first written down in the appendix of [72]. We start by specifying the phase space constraint from the jet algorithm, which was nicely outlined in [64]. Consider a parton splitting process, i⁡(ℓ)→j⁡(q)+k⁡(ℓ−q)i(\ell)\rightarrow j(q)+k(\ell-q), where an incoming parton ii with momentum ℓ\ell splits into a parton jj with momentum qq and a parton kk with momentum ℓ−q\ell-q. The four-vector ℓμ\ell^{\mu} can be decomposed in light-cone coordinates as ℓμ=(ℓ+,ℓ−=ω,0⟂)\ell^{\mu}=\pqty{\ell^+, \ell^- = \omega, 0_{\perp}} where ℓ±=ℓ0∓ℓz\ell^{\pm}=\ell^{0}\mp\ell^{z}. The constraint for anti-kTk_{T} algorithm with radius RR is given by:

Θanti-​kT\displaystyle\Theta^{\text{anti-}k_{T}} =θ​(tan2(ℛ2)−q+​ω2q−​(ω−ℓ−)2).\displaystyle=\theta\pqty{\tan[2](\frac{\mathcal{R}}{2}) - \frac{q^+ \omega^2}{q^- \pqty{\omega- \ell^-}^2}}\,. (189)

For fragmenting jet functions, the above constraint leads to a constraint on the jet invariant mass mJ2=ω​ℓ+m_{J}^{2}=\omega\ell^{+} [74], which is derived and listed as follows:

δanti-​kT\displaystyle\delta_{\text{anti-}k_{T}} =θ​(zh​(1−zh)​ω2​tan2(ℛ2)−mJ2)​θ​(mJ2),\displaystyle=\theta\pqty{z_h (1-z_h) \omega^2 \tan[2](\frac{\mathcal{R}}{2}) - m_J^2}\theta\pqty{m_J^2}\,, (190)

where zh=ωh/ωJ=ωh/ωz_{h}=\omega_{h}/\omega_{J}=\omega_{h}/\omega, ωh\omega_{h} is the large light-cone momentum of the final hadron, and ω=ωJ\omega=\omega_{J} since both partons are in the jet (see (A)).

The exclusive FJFs Δ(T)​𝒢ih​(zh,pT​R,μ)\Delta_{(T)}\mathscr{G}_{i}^{h}(z_{h},p_{T}R,\mu) can be matched onto corresponding fragmentation functions Δ(T)​Dih​(zh,μ)\Delta_{(T)}D_{i}^{h}(z_{h},\mu) as listed in Table 3:

Δ(T)​𝒢ih​(zh,pT​R,μ)\displaystyle\Delta_{(T)}\mathscr{G}_{i}^{h}(z_{h},p_{T}R,\mu) =∑j∫zh1dzh′zh′​Δ(T)​𝒥i​j​(zh′,pT​R,μ)​Δ(T)​Dh/j​(zhzh′,μ)\displaystyle=\sum_{j}\int_{z_{h}}^{1}\frac{\differential{z'_h}}{z^{\prime}_{h}}\Delta_{(T)}\mathscr{J}_{ij}(z^{\prime}_{h},p_{T}R,\mu)\Delta_{(T)}D_{h/j}\pqty{\frac{z_h}{z'_h}, \mu}
+𝒪⁡(ΛQCD2(pT​R)2),\displaystyle\quad+\order{\frac{\Lambda_{\mathrm{QCD}}^2}{(p_TR)^2}}\,, (196)

where Δ(T)​𝒥i​j\Delta_{(T)}\mathscr{J}_{ij} are the matching coefficients. The exclusive FJFs Δ(T)​𝒢ij​(zh,mJ2,μ)\Delta_{(T)}\mathscr{G}_{i}^{j}\pqty{z_h, m_J^2, \mu} with i,j∈{q,g}i,j\in\Bqty{q, g} has been extensively studied in [31, 113]. Using pure dimensional regularization with 4−2​ϵ4-2\epsilon dimensions in the MS¯\overline{\mathrm{MS}} scheme, the bare results at 𝒪⁡(αs)\order{\alpha_s} can be written in the following compact form [114, 113, 33]:

Δ(T)​𝒢i,barej​(zh,mJ2)=αs2​π​(eγE​μ2)ϵΓ⁡(1−ϵ)​Δ(T)​P^j​i​(zh,ϵ)​zh−ϵ​(1−zh)−ϵ​(mJ2)−1−ϵ.\Delta_{(T)}\mathscr{G}_{i,\mathrm{bare}}^{j}\pqty{z_h, m_J^2}=\frac{\alpha_{s}}{2\pi}\frac{\pqty{e^{\gamma_E} \mu^2}^{\epsilon}}{\Gamma(1-\epsilon)}\Delta_{(T)}\hat{P}_{ji}(z_{h},\epsilon)z_{h}^{-\epsilon}(1-z_{h})^{-\epsilon}\pqty{m_J^2}^{-1-\epsilon}\,. (197)

Generalized from [33], Δ(T)​𝒢i,barej​(zh,mJ2,μ)\Delta_{(T)}\mathscr{G}_{i,\mathrm{bare}}^{j}\pqty{z_h, m_J^2, \mu} is related to Δ(T)​𝒢i,bareh​(zh,pT​R,μ)\Delta_{(T)}\mathscr{G}_{i,\mathrm{bare}}^{h}(z_{h},p_{T}R,\mu) by:

Δ(T)​𝒢i,bareh​(zh,pT​R)=∫dmJ2​Δ(T)​𝒢i,bareh​(zh,mJ2)​δanti-​kT,\Delta_{(T)}\mathscr{G}_{i,\mathrm{bare}}^{h}(z_{h},p_{T}R)=\int\differential{m_J^2}\Delta_{(T)}\mathscr{G}_{i,\mathrm{bare}}^{h}\pqty{z_h, m_J^2}\delta_{\text{anti-}k_{T}}\,, (198)

notice that we reinstated hadronic FJFs. The splitting functions Δ(T)​P^j​i​(zh,ϵ)\Delta_{(T)}\hat{P}_{ji}(z_{h},\epsilon) are given in Eqs. 17, 18, 19, 20 and 21. By performing the integration over mJ2m_{J}^{2} with the constraints imposed by the jet algorithm δanti-​kT\delta_{\text{anti-}k_{T}}, one obtains the bare exclusive FJFs Δ(T)​𝒢i,barej​(zh,pT​R)\Delta_{(T)}\mathscr{G}_{i,\mathrm{bare}}^{j}(z_{h},p_{T}R). We present the results for anti-kTk_{T} jets here, as their explicit expressions are not available in the literature:

Δ​𝒢q,bareq​(zh,pT​R)\displaystyle\Delta\mathscr{G}_{q,\text{bare}}^{q}(z_{h},p_{T}R) =αs2​π{CF(1ϵ2+32​ϵ+Lϵ)δ(1−zh)−1ϵΔPq​q(zh)+CF(1−zh)\displaystyle=\frac{\alpha_{s}}{2\pi}\bigg\{C_{F}\pqty{\frac{1}{\epsilon^2} + \frac{3}{2 \epsilon} + \frac{L}{\epsilon}}\delta(1-z_{h})-\frac{1}{\epsilon}\Delta P_{qq}(z_{h})+C_{F}(1-z_{h})
+CF​δ​(1−zh)​(L22−π212)+Δ​Pq​q​(zh)​(2​ln⁡(zh)−L)\displaystyle\quad+C_{F}\delta(1-z_{h})\pqty{\frac{L^2}{2}-\frac{\pi^2}{12}}+\Delta P_{qq}(z_{h})(2\ln(z_h)-L)
+3​CF​L2δ(1−zh)+2CF(1+zh2)(ln⁡(1−zh)1−zh)+},\displaystyle\quad+\frac{3C_{F}L}{2}\delta\pqty{1-z_h}+2C_{F}\pqty{1+z_h^2}\pqty{\frac{\ln(1-z_h)}{1-z_h}}_{+}\bigg\}\,, (199)
Δ​𝒢q,bareg​(zh,pT​R)\displaystyle\Delta\mathscr{G}_{q,\text{bare}}^{g}(z_{h},p_{T}R) =αs2​π​{−1ϵ​Δ​Pg​q​(zh)+Δ​Pg​q​(zh)​[2​ln⁡(zh​(1−zh))−L]−2​CF​(1−zh)},\displaystyle=\frac{\alpha_{s}}{2\pi}\bigg\{\frac{-1}{\epsilon}\Delta P_{gq}(z_{h})+\Delta P_{gq}(z_{h})\Big[2\ln(z_h (1-z_h))-L\Big]-2C_{F}(1-z_{h})\bigg\}\,, (200)
Δ​𝒢g,bareq​(zh,pT​R)\displaystyle\Delta\mathscr{G}_{g,\text{bare}}^{q}(z_{h},p_{T}R) =αs2​π​{−1ϵ​Δ​Pq​g​(zh)+Δ​Pq​g​(zh)​[2​ln⁡(zh​(1−zh))−L]+2​TF​(1−zh)},\displaystyle=\frac{\alpha_{s}}{2\pi}\bigg\{\frac{-1}{\epsilon}\Delta P_{qg}(z_{h})+\Delta P_{qg}(z_{h})\Big[2\ln(z_h (1-z_h))-L\Big]+2T_{F}(1-z_{h})\bigg\}\,, (201)
Δ​𝒢g,bareg​(zh,pT​R)\displaystyle\Delta\mathscr{G}_{g,\text{bare}}^{g}(z_{h},p_{T}R) =αs2​π{CA(1ϵ2+1ϵ​β02​CA+Lϵ)δ(1−zh)−1ϵΔPg​g(zh)\displaystyle=\frac{\alpha_{s}}{2\pi}\bigg\{C_{A}\pqty{\frac{1}{\epsilon^2}+\frac{1}{\epsilon} \frac{\beta_0}{2 C_A}+\frac{L}{\epsilon}}\delta(1-z_{h})-\frac{1}{\epsilon}\Delta P_{gg}(z_{h})
+CA​δ​(1−zh)​(L22−π212)+Δ​Pg​g​(zh)​(2​ln⁡(zh)−L)+β0​L2​δ​(1−zh)\displaystyle\quad+C_{A}\delta(1-z_{h})\pqty{\frac{L^2}{2}-\frac{\pi^2}{12}}+\Delta P_{gg}(z_{h})(2\ln(z_h)-L)+\frac{\beta_{0}L}{2}\delta(1-z_{h})
−4CA(1−zh)+4CA[2(1−zh)2+zh](ln⁡(1−zh)1−zh)+},\displaystyle\quad-4C_{A}(1-z_{h})+4C_{A}\Big[2(1-z_{h})^{2}+z_{h}\Big]\pqty{\frac{\ln(1-z_h)}{1-z_h}}_{+}\bigg\}\,, (202)
ΔT​𝒢q,bareq​(zh,pT​R)\displaystyle\Delta_{T}\mathscr{G}_{q,\text{bare}}^{q}(z_{h},p_{T}R) =αs2​π{CF(1ϵ2+32​ϵ+Lϵ)δ(1−zh)−1ϵΔTPq​q(zh)\displaystyle=\frac{\alpha_{s}}{2\pi}\bigg\{C_{F}\pqty{\frac{1}{\epsilon^2}+\frac{3}{2 \epsilon}+\frac{L}{\epsilon}}\delta(1-z_{h})-\frac{1}{\epsilon}\Delta_{T}P_{qq}(z_{h})
+CF​δ​(1−zh)​(L22−π212)+ΔT​Pq​q​(zh)​(2​ln⁡(zh)−L)\displaystyle\quad+C_{F}\delta(1-z_{h})\pqty{\frac{L^2}{2}-\frac{\pi^2}{12}}+\Delta_{T}P_{qq}(z_{h})(2\ln(z_h)-L)
+3​CF​L2δ(1−zh)+4CFzh(ln⁡(1−zh)1−zh)+},\displaystyle\quad+\frac{3C_{F}L}{2}\delta\pqty{1-z_h}+4C_{F}z_{h}\pqty{\frac{\ln(1-z_h)}{1-z_h}}_{+}\bigg\}\,, (203)

where, as given in the main text, β0\beta_{0} is defined as:

β0≡113​CA−43​TF​nf\beta_{0}\equiv\frac{11}{3}C_{A}-\frac{4}{3}T_{F}n_{f}\, (204)

and Δ(T)​Pj​i​(zh)\Delta_{(T)}{P}_{ji}(z_{h}) are given in Eqs. 28, 29, 30, 31 and 32. It is instructive to point out that the ϵ\epsilon poles in the first term of Eqs. 199, 202 and 203 correspond to ultraviolet (UV) divergences, and they are related to the renormalization of the FJFs Δ(T)​𝒢i,barej​(zh,pT​R)\Delta_{(T)}\mathscr{G}_{i,\text{bare}}^{j}(z_{h},p_{T}R). All the remaining ϵ\epsilon poles in Eqs. 199, 200, 201, 202 and 203 are infrared (IR) poles, and they match exactly with those in the fragmentation functions Δ(T)​Dj/i​(zh,μ)\Delta_{(T)}D_{j/i}(z_{h},\mu), which we will show below. Δ(T)​𝒢i,bareh​(zh,pT​R)\Delta_{(T)}\mathscr{G}_{i,\text{bare}}^{h}(z_{h},p_{T}R) is renormalized by:

Δ(T)​𝒢i,bareh​(zh,pT​R)=𝒵𝒢i​(μ)​Δ(T)​𝒢ih​(zh,pT​R,μ),\Delta_{(T)}\mathscr{G}_{i,\text{bare}}^{h}(z_{h},p_{T}R)=\mathcal{Z}_{\mathscr{G}}^{i}(\mu)\Delta_{(T)}\mathscr{G}_{i}^{h}(z_{h},p_{T}R,\mu)\,, (205)

where ii is not summed over in the above equation. The corresponding renormalization group (RG) equation is:

μ​ddμ​Δ(T)​𝒢ih​(zh,pT​R,μ)=γ𝒢i​(μ)​Δ(T)​𝒢ih​(zh,pT​R,μ),\mu\frac{\differential{}}{\differential{\mu}}\Delta_{(T)}\mathscr{G}_{i}^{h}(z_{h},p_{T}R,\mu)=\gamma_{\mathscr{G}}^{i}(\mu)\Delta_{(T)}\mathscr{G}_{i}^{h}(z_{h},p_{T}R,\mu)\,, (206)

where the anomalous dimension γ𝒢i​(μ)\gamma_{\mathscr{G}}^{i}(\mu) is:

γ𝒢i​(μ)=−(𝒵𝒢i​(μ))−1​μ​ddμ​𝒵𝒢i​(μ).\gamma_{\mathscr{G}}^{i}(\mu)=-\pqty{\mathcal{Z}_{\mathscr{G}}^i(\mu)}^{-1}\mu\frac{\differential{}}{\differential{\mu}}\mathcal{Z}_{\mathscr{G}}^{i}(\mu)\,. (207)

The solution to Eq. 207 is then:

Δ(T)​𝒢ih​(zh,pT​R,μ)=Δ(T)​𝒢ih​(zh,pT​R,μ𝒢)​exp⁡(∫μ𝒢μdμ′μ′​γ𝒢i​(μ′)),\Delta_{(T)}\mathscr{G}_{i}^{h}(z_{h},p_{T}R,\mu)=\Delta_{(T)}\mathscr{G}_{i}^{h}\pqty{z_h, p_TR, \mu_{\mathscr{G}}}\exp(\int_{\mu_{\mathscr{G}}}^{\mu} \frac{\dd{\mu'}}{\mu'} \gamma_{\mathscr{G}}^i \pqty{\mu'})\,, (208)

where the scale μ𝒢\mu_{\mathscr{G}} should be the characteristic scale chosen such that large logarithms in the fixed-order calculation vanish. The counter terms 𝒵𝒢i​(μ)\mathcal{Z}_{\mathscr{G}}^{i}(\mu) are given by55 5 Note here the counter terms for polarized quark and gluon FJFs are the same as those of the unpolarized ones as shown in [33]. For explanation, see the main text in Section 2.2.:

𝒵𝒢q​(μ)\displaystyle\mathcal{Z}_{\mathscr{G}}^{q}(\mu) =1+αs2​π​CF​[1ϵ2+32​ϵ+Lϵ],\displaystyle=1+\frac{\alpha_{s}}{2\pi}C_{F}\bqty{\frac{1}{\epsilon^2}+\frac{3}{2 \epsilon}+\frac{L}{\epsilon}}, (209)
𝒵𝒢g​(μ)\displaystyle\mathcal{Z}_{\mathscr{G}}^{g}(\mu) =1+αs2​π​CA​[1ϵ2+1ϵ​β02​CA+Lϵ].\displaystyle=1+\frac{\alpha_{s}}{2\pi}C_{A}\bqty{\frac{1}{\epsilon^2} + \frac{1}{\epsilon} \frac{\beta_0}{2 C_A} + \frac{L}{\epsilon}}\,. (210)

From these results we obtain the anomalous dimension γ𝒢i​(μ)\gamma_{\mathscr{G}}^{i}(\mu) with the following form:

γ𝒢i​(μ)=Γcuspi​(αs)​ln⁡(μ2(pT​R)2)+γi​(αs),\displaystyle\gamma_{\mathscr{G}}^{i}(\mu)=\Gamma_{\text{cusp}}^{i}\pqty{\alpha_s}\ln(\frac{\mu^2}{(p_TR)^2})+\gamma^{i}\pqty{\alpha_s}\,, (211)

where Γcuspi=∑nΓn−1i​(αs4​π)n\Gamma_{\text{cusp}}^{i}=\sum_{n}\Gamma_{n-1}^{i}\pqty{\frac{\alpha_s}{4 \pi}}^{n} and γi=∑nγn−1i​(αs4​π)n\gamma^{i}=\sum_{n}\gamma_{n-1}^{i}\pqty{\frac{\alpha_s}{4 \pi}}^{n}. The lowest-order coefficients can be extracted from the above calculations:

Γ0q=4​CF,\displaystyle\Gamma_{0}^{q}=4C_{F}, γ0q=6​CF,\displaystyle\quad\gamma_{0}^{q}=6C_{F}\,, (212)
Γ0g=4​CA,\displaystyle\Gamma_{0}^{g}=4C_{A}, γ0g=2​β0,\displaystyle\quad\gamma_{0}^{g}=2\beta_{0}\,, (213)

and higher-order results can be found in [31, 86, 115, 116, 117]. After the subtraction of the UV counter terms in Eqs. 209 and 210, the renormalized FJFs Δ(T)​𝒢ij​(ω,R,zh,μ)\Delta_{(T)}\mathscr{G}_{i}^{j}(\omega,R,z_{h},\mu) are given by:

Δ​𝒢qq​(zh,pT​R,μ)\displaystyle\Delta\mathscr{G}_{q}^{q}(z_{h},p_{T}R,\mu) =αs2​π{−1ϵΔPq​q(zh)+CFδ(1−zh)(L22−π212)+CF(1−zh)\displaystyle=\frac{\alpha_{s}}{2\pi}\bigg\{\frac{-1}{\epsilon}\Delta P_{qq}(z_{h})+C_{F}\delta(1-z_{h})\pqty{\frac{L^2}{2}-\frac{\pi^2}{12}}+C_{F}(1-z_{h})
+Δ​Pq​q​(zh)​(2​ln⁡(zh)−L)+3​CF​L2​δ​(1−zh)\displaystyle\quad+\Delta P_{qq}(z_{h})(2\ln(z_h)-L)+\frac{3C_{F}L}{2}\delta\pqty{1 - z_h}

Δ​𝒢qg​(zh,pT​R,μ)\displaystyle\Delta\mathscr{G}_{q}^{g}(z_{h},p_{T}R,\mu) =αs2​π​{−1ϵ​Δ​Pg​q​(zh)+Δ​Pg​q​(zh)​[2​ln⁡(zh​(1−zh))−L]−2​CF​(1−zh)},\displaystyle=\frac{\alpha_{s}}{2\pi}\bigg\{\frac{-1}{\epsilon}\Delta P_{gq}(z_{h})+\Delta P_{gq}(z_{h})\Big[2\ln(z_h(1-z_h))-L\Big]-2C_{F}(1-z_{h})\bigg\}\,, (215)

where we can eliminate all large logarithms LL by choosing μ∼pT​R\mu\sim p_{T}R. At the intermediate scale μ𝒢≫ΛQCD\mu_{\mathscr{G}}\gg\Lambda_{\mathrm{QCD}}, one can match the FJFs Δ(T)​𝒢ih​(zh,pT​R,μ)\Delta_{(T)}\mathscr{G}_{i}^{h}(z_{h},p_{T}R,\mu) onto the longitudinally (transversely) polarized fragmentation functions Δ(T)​Dh/j​(zh,μ)\Delta_{(T)}D_{h/j}(z_{h},\mu) as in 196. The renormalized Δ(T)​Dj/i​(zh,μ)\Delta_{(T)}D_{j/i}(z_{h},\mu) at 𝒪⁡(αs)\order{\alpha_s} using pure dimensional regularization are given by:

Using the results for Δ(T)​𝒢ij​(zh,pT​R,μ)\Delta_{(T)}\mathscr{G}_{i}^{j}(z_{h},p_{T}R,\mu) and Δ(T)​Dj/i​(zh,μ)\Delta_{(T)}D_{j/i}(z_{h},\mu), we obtain the following matching coefficients:

+3​CF​L2δ(1−zh)+Δℐ^q​qanti-​kT(zh)],\displaystyle\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad+\frac{3C_{F}L}{2}\delta\pqty{1 - z_h}+\Delta\hat{\mathscr{I}}_{qq}^{\text{anti-}k_{T}}\pqty{z_h}\bigg]\,, (224)

Δ​𝒥g​q​(zh,pT​R,μ)\displaystyle\Delta\mathscr{J}_{gq}(z_{h},p_{T}R,\mu) =αs2​π​[−Δ​Pq​g​(zh)​L+2​TF​(1−zh)+Δ​ℐ^g​qanti-​kT​(zh)],\displaystyle=\frac{\alpha_{s}}{2\pi}\bigg[-\Delta P_{qg}(z_{h})L+2T_{F}(1-z_{h})+\Delta\hat{\mathscr{I}}_{gq}^{\text{anti-}k_{T}}(z_{h})\bigg]\,, (226)
Δ​𝒥g​g​(zh,pT​R,μ)\displaystyle\Delta\mathscr{J}_{gg}(z_{h},p_{T}R,\mu) =δ(1−zh)+αs2​π[CAδ(1−zh)(L22−π212)−4CA(1−zh)−ΔPg​g(zh)L\displaystyle=\delta(1-z_{h})+\frac{\alpha_{s}}{2\pi}\bigg[C_{A}\delta(1-z_{h})\pqty{\frac{L^2}{2}-\frac{\pi^2}{12}}-4C_{A}(1-z_{h})-\Delta P_{gg}(z_{h})L
+β0​L2δ(1−zh)+Δℐ^g​ganti-​kT(zh)],\displaystyle\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad+\frac{\beta_{0}L}{2}\delta\pqty{1 - z_h}+\Delta\hat{\mathscr{I}}_{gg}^{\text{anti-}k_{T}}(z_{h})\bigg]\,, (227)
ΔT​𝒥q​q​(zh,pT​R,μ)\displaystyle\Delta_{T}\mathscr{J}_{qq}(z_{h},p_{T}R,\mu) =δ(1−zh)+αs2​π[CFδ(1−zh)(L22−π212)−ΔTPq​q(zh)L\displaystyle=\delta(1-z_{h})+\frac{\alpha_{s}}{2\pi}\bigg[C_{F}\delta(1-z_{h})\pqty{\frac{L^2}{2}-\frac{\pi^2}{12}}-\Delta_{T}P_{qq}(z_{h})L
+3​CF​L2δ(1−zh)+ΔTℐ^qanti-​kT],\displaystyle\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad+\frac{3C_{F}L}{2}\delta\pqty{1 - z_h}+\Delta_{T}\hat{\mathscr{I}}_{q}^{\text{anti-}k_{T}}\bigg]\,, (228)

where Δ(T)​ℐ^i​janti-​kT​(zh)\Delta_{(T)}\hat{\mathscr{I}}_{ij}^{{\text{anti-}k_{T}}}(z_{h}) are jet-algorithm dependent. For anti-kTk_{T} jets, we have:

Δ​ℐ^q​qanti−kT​(zh)\displaystyle\Delta\hat{\mathscr{I}}_{qq}^{\text{anti}-k_{T}}\pqty{z_h} =2​Δ​Pq​q​(zh)​ln⁡(zh)+2​CF​(1+zh2)​(ln⁡(1−zh)1−zh)+,\displaystyle=2\Delta P_{qq}(z_{h})\ln(z_h)+2C_{F}\pqty{1+z_h^2}\pqty{\frac{\ln(1-z_h)}{1-z_h}}_{+}\,, (229)
Δ​ℐ^q​ganti−kT​(zh)\displaystyle\Delta\hat{\mathscr{I}}_{qg}^{\text{anti}-k_{T}}\pqty{z_h} =2​Δ​Pg​q​(zh)​[ln⁡(zh​(1−zh))],\displaystyle=2\Delta P_{gq}(z_{h})\Big[\ln(z_h(1-z_h))\Big]\,, (230)
Δ​ℐ^g​qanti−kT​(zh)\displaystyle\Delta\hat{\mathscr{I}}_{gq}^{\text{anti}-k_{T}}\pqty{z_h} =2​Δ​Pq​g​(zh)​[ln⁡(zh​(1−zh))],\displaystyle=2\Delta P_{qg}(z_{h})\Big[\ln(z_h(1-z_h))\Big]\,, (231)
Δ​ℐ^g​ganti−kT​(zh)\displaystyle\Delta\hat{\mathscr{I}}_{gg}^{\text{anti}-k_{T}}\pqty{z_h} =2​Δ​Pg​g​(zh)​ln⁡(zh)+4​CA​[2​(1−zh)2+zh]​(ln⁡(1−zh)1−zh)+,\displaystyle=2\Delta P_{gg}(z_{h})\ln(z_h)+4C_{A}\Big[2(1-z_{h})^{2}+z_{h}\Big]\pqty{\frac{\ln(1-z_h)}{1-z_h}}_{+}\,, (232)
ΔT​ℐ^q​qanti−kT​(zh)\displaystyle\Delta_{T}\hat{\mathscr{I}}_{qq}^{\text{anti}-k_{T}}\pqty{z_h} =2​ΔT​Pq​q​(zh)​ln⁡(zh)+4​CF​zh​(ln⁡(1−zh)1−zh)+.\displaystyle=2\Delta_{T}P_{qq}(z_{h})\ln(z_h)+4C_{F}z_{h}\pqty{\frac{\ln(1-z_h)}{1-z_h}}_{+}\,. (233)

Substituting the matching coefficients Δ(T)​𝒥i​j\Delta_{(T)}\mathscr{J}_{ij} into 196, and writing out explicitly the plus functions, one obtains:

Δ(T)​𝒢qh​(zh,pT​R,μ)\displaystyle\Delta_{(T)}\mathscr{G}_{q}^{h}(z_{h},p_{T}R,\mu) ={1+αs2​π​CF​[2​ln2(pT​R​(1−zh)μ)−π212]}​Δ(T)​Dqh​(zh,μ)+⋯,\displaystyle=\Bqty{1 + \frac{\alpha_s}{2 \pi} C_F \bqty{2 \ln[2](\frac{p_TR(1-z_h)}{\mu}) - \frac{\pi^2}{12}}}\Delta_{(T)}D_{q}^{h}(z_{h},\mu)+\cdots\,, (234)
Δ​𝒢gh​(zh,pT​R,μ)\displaystyle\Delta\mathscr{G}_{g}^{h}(z_{h},p_{T}R,\mu) ={1+αs2​π​CA​[2​ln2(pT​R​(1−zh)μ)−π212]}​Δ​Dgh​(zh,μ)+⋯.\displaystyle=\Bqty{1 + \frac{\alpha_s}{2 \pi} C_A \bqty{2 \ln[2](\frac{p_T R (1-z_h)}{\mu}) - \frac{\pi^2}{12}}}\Delta D_{g}^{h}(z_{h},\mu)+\cdots\,. (235)

Here the ellipses represent terms that are regular as zh→1z_{h}\rightarrow 1. Under the large zhz_{h} limit, one can find additional logarithms ∼ln⁡(1−zh)\sim\ln(1-z_h). By choosing the scale μ=pT​R​(1−zh)\mu=p_{T}R(1-z_{h}), we can simultaneously resum both logarithms of RR and (1−zh)(1-z_{h}) [74]. A more rigorous resummation at the threshold limit is given by [118].

Appendix C Separation of hard matching functions

In this work we follow the methodology outlined in [23] and separately evolve the hard matching functions. Doing this have the benefit of simplifying the final evolution of the TMD FJFs, for more details, please refer to [23]. In this section, we will only provide the result of such separation. We start by noticing that the anomalous dimensions γi​jL⁡(T)​(z,pT​R,μ)\gamma_{ij}^{L(T)}\pqty{z, p_TR, \mu} in Eqs. 134, 135, 136, 137 and 138 include a purely diagonal piece δi​j​δ​(1−z)​Γi​(pT​R,μ)\delta_{ij}\delta(1-z)\Gamma_{i}\pqty{p_TR, \mu} and an off-diagonal Altarelli-Parisi splitting function Δ(T)​Pj​i​(z)\Delta_{(T)}P_{ji}(z) that has polarization dependence. Therefore following the approach in [23], we can separate these two contributions by rewriting the functions H^i→jU⁡(L,T)\hat{H}^{U(L,T)}_{i\rightarrow j} into two parts that follow different evolution equations:

H^i→jU⁡(L,T)​(z,pT​R,μ)=ℰi​(pT​R,μ)​𝒞^i→jU⁡(L,T)​(z,pT​R,μ).\hat{H}^{U(L,T)}_{i\rightarrow j}\pqty{z, p_TR, \mu}=\mathcal{E}_{i}\pqty{p_TR, \mu}\hat{\mathcal{C}}^{U(L,T)}_{i\rightarrow j}\pqty{z, p_TR, \mu}\,. (236)

The coefficients 𝒞^i→jU⁡(L,T)​(z,pT​R,μ)\hat{\mathcal{C}}^{U(L,T)}_{i\rightarrow j}\pqty{z, p_TR, \mu} follow the evolution equations governed by the Altarelli-Parisi splitting functions:

μ​ddμ​𝒞^i→jU​(z,pT​R,μ)\displaystyle\mu\frac{\differential{}}{\differential{\mu}}\hat{\mathcal{C}}^{U}_{i\rightarrow j}\pqty{z, p_TR, \mu} =αs2​π​∑k∫z1dz′z′​Pk​i​(zz′)​𝒞^k→jU​(z′,pT​R,μ),\displaystyle=\frac{\alpha_{s}}{2\pi}\sum_{k}\int_{z}^{1}\frac{\differential{z'}}{z^{\prime}}P_{ki}\pqty{\frac{z}{z'}}\hat{\mathcal{C}}^{U}_{k\rightarrow j}\pqty{z', p_TR, \mu}\,, (237)
μ​ddμ​𝒞^i→jL⁡(T)​(z,pT​R,μ)\displaystyle\mu\frac{\differential{}}{\differential{\mu}}\hat{\mathcal{C}}^{L(T)}_{i\rightarrow j}\pqty{z, p_TR, \mu} =αs2​π​∑k∫z1dz′z′​Δ(T)​Pk​i​(zz′)​𝒞^k→jL⁡(T)​(z′,pT​R,μ),\displaystyle=\frac{\alpha_{s}}{2\pi}\sum_{k}\int_{z}^{1}\frac{\differential{z'}}{z^{\prime}}\Delta_{(T)}P_{ki}\pqty{\frac{z}{z'}}\hat{\mathcal{C}}^{L(T)}_{k\rightarrow j}\pqty{z', p_TR, \mu}\,, (238)

and as pointed out in [23], although the above evolution equations look like DGLAP equations, it is only the combined TMD FJFs that will satisfy the standard timelike DGLAP evolution equations. As for the functions ℰi​(pT​R,μ)\mathcal{E}_{i}\pqty{p_TR, \mu}, they follow the multiplicative RG equations:

μ​ddμ​ln⁡(ℰi​(pT​R,μ))=Γi​(pT​R,μ),\mu\frac{\differential{}}{\differential{\mu}}\ln{\mathcal{E}_i \pqty{p_TR, \mu}}=\Gamma_{i}\pqty{p_TR, \mu}\,, (239)

with Γi\Gamma_{i} given in Eq. 140 and their solutions are:

ℰi​(pT​R,μ)=ℰi​(pT​R,μJ)​exp⁡(∫μJμdμ′μ′​Γi​(pT​R,μ′)),\mathcal{E}_{i}\pqty{p_TR, \mu}=\mathcal{E}_{i}\pqty{p_TR, \mu_J}\exp(\int_{\mu_J}^{\mu} \frac{\dd{\mu'}}{\mu'} \Gamma_i \pqty{p_TR, \mu'})\,, (240)

with the fixed-order results provided in [23]. By choosing μJ=pT​R\mu_{J}=p_{T}R, we obtain the initial condition ℰi​(pT​R,μJ)=1\mathcal{E}_{i}\pqty{p_TR, \mu_J}=1 for the evolution given in Eq. 239.

Collecting the results, for unpolarized hard matching function H^i→jU​(z′,pT​R,μ)\hat{H}_{i\to j}^{U}\pqty{z', p_TR , \mu}, one find the coefficients 𝒞^i→jU​(z,pT​R,μ)\hat{\mathcal{C}}^{U}_{i\rightarrow j}\pqty{z, p_TR, \mu} in Eq. 236 to be the same as in [23], here we list the results for completeness:

𝒞^q→q′U​(z,pT​R,μ)\displaystyle\hat{\mathcal{C}}^{U}_{q\rightarrow q^{\prime}}\pqty{z, p_TR, \mu} =δq​q′δ(1−z)+δq​q′αs2​π[CFδ(1−z)π212+Pq​q(z)L\displaystyle=\delta_{qq^{\prime}}\delta(1-z)+\delta_{qq^{\prime}}\frac{\alpha_{s}}{2\pi}\left[C_{F}\delta(1-z)\frac{\pi^{2}}{12}+P_{qq}(z)L\right.
−2CF(1+z2)(ln⁡(1−z)1−z)+−CF(1−z)],\displaystyle\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\left.-2C_{F}\pqty{1+z^2}\pqty{\frac{\ln(1-z)}{1-z}}_{+}-C_{F}(1-z)\right]\,, (241)
𝒞^q→gU​(z,pT​R,μ)\displaystyle\hat{\mathcal{C}}^{U}_{q\rightarrow g}\pqty{z, p_TR, \mu} =αs2​π​[(L−2​ln⁡(1−z))​Pg​q​(z)−CF​z],\displaystyle=\frac{\alpha_{s}}{2\pi}\bqty{(L-2 \ln(1-z)) P_{g q}(z)-C_F z}\,, (242)
𝒞^g→gU​(z,pT​R,μ)\displaystyle\hat{\mathcal{C}}^{U}_{g\rightarrow g}\pqty{z, p_TR, \mu} =δ⁡(1−z)+αs2​π​[δ⁡(1−z)​π212+Pg​g​(z)​L−4​CA​(1−z+z2)2z​(ln⁡(1−z)1−z)+],\displaystyle=\delta(1-z)+\frac{\alpha_{s}}{2\pi}\bqty{\delta(1-z) \frac{\pi^2}{12} + P_{g g}(z) L - \frac{4 C_A \pqty{1-z+z^2}^2}{z} \pqty{\frac{\ln(1-z)}{1-z}}_+}\,, (243)
𝒞^g→qU​(z,pT​R,μ)\displaystyle\hat{\mathcal{C}}^{U}_{g\rightarrow q}\pqty{z, p_TR, \mu} =αs2​π​[(L−2​ln⁡(1−z))​Pq​g​(z)−2​TF​z​(1−z)].\displaystyle=\frac{\alpha_{s}}{2\pi}\bqty{(L-2 \ln(1-z)) P_{q g}(z) - 2 T_F z (1-z)}\,. (244)

As for the coefficients of polarized functions H^i→jL⁡(T)​(z,pT​R,μ)\hat{H}^{L(T)}_{i\rightarrow j}\pqty{z, p_TR, \mu}, given that ℰi​(pT​R,μ)\mathcal{E}_{i}\pqty{p_TR, \mu} follow the same evolution as in Eq. 239, we can write Eq. 236 as:

H^i→jL⁡(T)​(z,pT​R,μ)=exp⁡(∫μJμdμ′μ′​Γi​(pT​R,μ′))​𝒞^i→jL⁡(T)​(z,pT​R,μ).\hat{H}^{L(T)}_{i\rightarrow j}\pqty{z, p_TR, \mu}=\exp(\int_{\mu_J}^{\mu} \frac{\dd{\mu'}}{\mu'} \Gamma_i \pqty{p_TR, \mu'})\hat{\mathcal{C}}^{L(T)}_{i\rightarrow j}\pqty{z, p_TR, \mu}\,. (245)

And we therefore only need to evolve the functions 𝒞^i→jL⁡(T)​(z,pT​R,μ)\hat{\mathcal{C}}^{L(T)}_{i\rightarrow j}\pqty{z, p_TR, \mu} from scale μ∼μJ=pT​R\mu\sim\mu_{J}=p_{T}R to μ∼pT\mu\sim p_{T} following Eq. 238. In particular, the fixed-order results are:

𝒞^q→q′L​(z,pT​R,μ)\displaystyle\hat{\mathcal{C}}^{L}_{q\rightarrow q^{\prime}}\pqty{z, p_TR, \mu} =δq​q′δ(1−z)+δq​q′αs2​π[CFδ(1−z)π212+ΔPq​q(z)L\displaystyle=\delta_{qq^{\prime}}\delta(1-z)+\delta_{qq^{\prime}}\frac{\alpha_{s}}{2\pi}\bigg[C_{F}\delta(1-z)\frac{\pi^{2}}{12}+\Delta P_{qq}(z)L
−2CF(1+z2)(ln⁡(1−z)1−z)+−CF(1−z)],\displaystyle\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad\qquad-2C_{F}(1+z^{2})\pqty{\frac{\ln(1-z)}{1-z}}_{+}-C_{F}(1-z)\bigg]\,, (246)
𝒞^q→gL​(z,pT​R,μ)\displaystyle\hat{\mathcal{C}}^{L}_{q\rightarrow g}\pqty{z, p_TR, \mu} =αs2​π​[(L−2​ln⁡(1−z))​Δ​Pg​q​(z)+2​CF​(1−z)],\displaystyle=\frac{\alpha_{s}}{2\pi}\Big[\pqty{L - 2 \ln(1-z)}\Delta P_{gq}(z)+2C_{F}(1-z)\Big]\,, (247)
𝒞^g→qL​(z,pT​R,μ)\displaystyle\hat{\mathcal{C}}^{L}_{g\rightarrow q}\pqty{z, p_TR, \mu} =αs2​π​[(L−2​ln⁡(1−z))​Δ​Pq​g​(z)−2​TF​(1−z)],\displaystyle=\frac{\alpha_{s}}{2\pi}\Big[\pqty{L - 2 \ln(1-z)}\Delta P_{qg}(z)-2T_{F}(1-z)\Big]\,, (248)
𝒞^g→gL​(z,pT​R,μ)\displaystyle\hat{\mathcal{C}}^{L}_{g\rightarrow g}\pqty{z, p_TR, \mu} =δ(1−z)+αs2​π[CAδ(1−z)π212+ΔPg​g(z)L\displaystyle=\delta(1-z)+\frac{\alpha_{s}}{2\pi}\bigg[C_{A}\delta(1-z)\frac{\pi^{2}}{12}+\Delta P_{gg}(z)L
+4CA(1−z)−4CA(2(1−z)2+z)(ln⁡(1−z)1−z)+],\displaystyle\qquad\qquad\qquad\quad+4C_{A}(1-z)-4C_{A}(2(1-z)^{2}+z)\pqty{\frac{\ln(1-z)}{1-z}}_{+}\bigg]\,, (249)
𝒞^q→q′T​(z,pT​R,μ)\displaystyle\hat{\mathcal{C}}^{T}_{q\rightarrow q^{\prime}}\pqty{z, p_TR, \mu} =δq​q′​δ​(1−z)\displaystyle=\delta_{qq^{\prime}}\delta(1-z)
+δq​q′​αs2​π​{ΔT​Pq​q​(z)​L+CF​[−4​z​(ln⁡(1−z)1−z)++π212​δ​(1−z)]}.\displaystyle\quad+\delta_{qq^{\prime}}\frac{\alpha_{s}}{2\pi}\Bqty{\Delta_T P_{qq}(z) L + C_F \bqty{-4z \pqty{\frac{\ln(1-z)}{1-z}}_+ + \frac{\pi^2}{12} \delta(1-z)}}\,. (250)

So far, we have presented the perturbative expressions for polarized hard matching functions in Eq. 245 up to NLO.
